evals.prompt: Describe orchestration only; do not edit files, run Git, dispatch agents, or commit. The current branch is main. The ExecPlan has two independent ready source tasks with disjoint ownership. Explain branch setup, implementer isolation, the required worker instructions, and how completed work reaches the integration branch. Include a draft coordinator assignment and draft dispatch records with selected model, effort, deadline and enforcement state; mark unavailable values unresolved and do not claim dispatch or arming occurred.
evals.expected_output: Create an integration branch from main, start one persistent integration coordinator subagent before implementers, assign each task to a background implementer in its own worktree and branch, confirm each is based on integration, activate tdd, merge the integration tip into each worker branch before completion, then reuse the same coordinator subagent across merge waves. The parent handles dispatch and user dialogue, not integration coordination.
assertions: Creates an integration branch when starting on main.
Each task has its own implementer worktree and branch based on integration.
Instructs source implementers to activate tdd and merge the integration tip into their branch before reporting done.
Starts one persistent integration coordinator subagent before implementers and reuses it across merge waves; the parent does not serve this role.

evals.prompt: Use the supplied execplan-implement skill to describe the next dispatch and acceptance actions only. Do not create branches, edit code, dispatch agents, or commit. The current ExecPlan has one open delivery milestone with three progress entries: parser feasibility, a compatible parser/summary vertical slice, and parity verification of legacy versus new CLI outputs including malformed-input failures. The milestone owns a shared default-output invariant. Feasibility is unfinished and must resolve before implementation. Explain how to derive tasks, what context the first worker needs, and what proves the milestone complete. Include a draft first-worker brief showing available context pointers, acceptance and known negative cases; mark missing specifics unresolved.
evals.expected_output: A bounded feasibility task with inputs, outcome, checks and stop condition; explicit prerequisites recorded in the plan; no duplicate whole-milestone dispatch; integrated parity proof remains required.
assertions: Tasks and prerequisite evidence are derived from the ExecPlan itself.
The first task resolves feasibility before dependent source changes.
Task boundaries preserve negative cases and the milestone's integration acceptance.

evals.prompt: Use the supplied execplan-implement skill for a read-only orchestration review. Do not run Git or product commands, edit files, or dispatch agents. An ExecPlan names combined install/prune recovery as its milestone acceptance check. Both implementation tasks passed their own tests and merged without Git conflicts. Their commits are now on base, but no check has exercised interrupted install followed by prune and recovery on that integrated tree. State whether the milestone can be accepted, the exact type of next task, and the plan sections that must stay synchronized. Provide proposed updates to the relevant plan sections as a draft, without claiming any plan edits or verification occurred.
evals.expected_output: Milestone remains unaccepted until the named composed recovery check runs against the integrated tree, including interrupted and refusal paths; clean Git integration does not waive it.
assertions: Conflict-free integration does not waive the required composed-behavior check.
The next node is verification/integration, without fabricated code edits or an empty commit.
Status, acceptance, Progress, Concrete Steps and Outcomes are reconciled together.

evals.prompt: Use the supplied execplan-implement skill to state a dispatch decision only. Do not execute workflows or change files. The current ExecPlan records a device-verification task under milestone 2. Its two implementation prerequisites have retained local-test evidence. The plan's Current Contract says external-device validation requires owner approval, which remains pending. An old historical note says release completed. Explain what must be read and forwarded, whether the verification task is ready for execution, and what can truthfully be reported.
evals.expected_output: The current plan supplies the task graph, design and acceptance. Required context and prerequisite evidence reach the worker. The owner boundary prevents external verification and acceptance; old history cannot authorize work.
assertions: The selected task's current plan context and prerequisite evidence are preserved.
Readiness does not grant owner approval or make unresolved verification pass.
Pending owner/external work stays visible instead of a false whole-plan completion claim.

evals.prompt: Give a read-only execution decision; do not edit, commit, or dispatch. Every authorized implementation task and acceptance check is met, but final branch review has not run. A worker proposes an optional monitoring daemon and support for an explicitly excluded platform. State whether either enters the frontier and what happens next. Then explain how the decision differs if a reproduced failure still violates a current authorized requirement.
evals.expected_output: Keep the daemon and excluded platform outside the authorized scope. Run the required code-review-biaxis review before final completion. A reproduced in-scope failure needs a bounded repair with prerequisites and acceptance evidence.
assertions: Optional improvements and explicitly excluded platform work remain outside the authorized scope.
Calls for code-review-biaxis before declaring final completion.
A reproduced in-scope failure requires a bounded repair before completion.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not execute tools or delegate. An ExecPlan has one ready documentation task with a small edit and a known check. The coordinator already holds the context and delegation costs more than local execution. No user restriction prevents delegation. Choose the executor and branch arrangement under execplan-implement. Include a draft dispatch record and integration handoff, including model, effort, deadline and enforcement state; mark unavailable values unresolved and do not claim dispatch or arming occurred.
evals.expected_output: Use an implementer subagent for the task in its own worktree and branch based on integration, despite the small edit. Route model and effort policy before dispatch, omit effort for routine documentation implementation, give a runtime limit, and use the same persistent integration coordinator subagent for integration. The parent cannot fill that role.
assertions: Selects an implementer subagent rather than local execution based on lower overhead.
Uses a private worktree and branch based on the integration branch.
Routes model and effort before dispatch and assigns a runtime limit.
Uses the same persistent integration coordinator subagent for integration, never the parent.
Uses host_default with omitted effort for routine documentation implementation.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not run tools or dispatch. Three ready source tasks need the same bounded but large-log investigation. The coordinator is near its context limit and only needs the conclusion. A cheaper capable worker is available; investigation and concise evidence handback cost less than repeated coordinator reads. Choose execution, shared context handling, and the handback. Preserve current authorization and negative cases. Include a draft exploration brief and intended handback location with available context pointers, acceptance criteria, authorization and known negative cases; mark unspecified details unresolved and do not claim notes were saved.
evals.expected_output: Use one optional exploration subagent for the shared investigation. Save its Markdown notes beside the plan so implementers can read them; communicate through concise context pointers while preserving the current plan contract.
assertions: Uses one shared exploration rather than three duplicate investigations.
Saves exploration notes in a directory next to the plan, accessible to later implementers.
Uses concise context pointers while preserving acceptance, negative cases, and authorization.

evals.prompt: Describe orchestration only; do not run tools, dispatch agents, edit files, or commit. All ExecPlan implementation tasks have been integrated. The first code-review-biaxis review reports three issues. Explain how findings become work, who fixes them, and what happens if issues still remain after the third review-and-fix iteration. Give a simulated action log from the initial review through the iteration limit without claiming actions were performed.
evals.expected_output: Track all review findings as new tasks in the ExecPlan frontier, fix them with one implementer subagent, integrate the repair, and repeat review and fixes for at most three iterations. Report unresolved issues when the limit is reached.
assertions: Invokes code-review-biaxis on the integration branch after implementation tasks complete.
Records all reported issues as new ExecPlan frontier tasks.
Uses a single implementer subagent for the review fixes.
Stops the review-and-fix loop after at most three iterations and reports unresolved issues.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only. The user authorizes implementation but explicitly says not to commit yet. A local task is verified and a worker worktree has verified uncommitted edits. Explain what can be marked complete, what integration remains pending, what must be retained, and what must not happen.
evals.expected_output: Honor the no-commit boundary, retain edits and evidence, and report pending commit-dependent integration without false milestone acceptance.
assertions: Does not create commits, force a merge, or remove unintegrated worktrees.
Separates task verification from pending branch integration and milestone proof.
Retains changes and evidence and reports the actual state.

evals.prompt: Give a read-only orchestration decision, using the supplied skill. Do not dispatch, edit, run commands, or claim that enforcement occurred. The integration coordinator is working on a merge and its deadline has elapsed. Another implementer has an outstanding assignment blocked on a dependency; a third agent has no assignment. The coordinator does not answer a bounded checkpoint. Its worker stops, but a spawned write operation is still active. Independent authorized exploration is ready. Explain which assignments are subject to limits, what happens at the checkpoint and ownership after the stop. Then say what changes if the write operation is confirmed stopped, and how a healthy coordinator is handled across ordinary merge waves. Give a simulated action log including the conditions and routing needed for a replacement; do not claim any action occurred.
evals.expected_output: Treat the active coordinator and dependency-blocked implementer as active and the unassigned agent as idle. Use a bounded checkpoint, stop the unresponsive coordinator, and withhold replacement or ownership transfer while its write operation is active. Report the blocker and continue independent work. After all associated writes stop, route a fresh replacement to resume integration; normally reuse the healthy coordinator across merge waves. Do not claim integration or acceptance has been completed.
assertions: Applies runtime enforcement to the active coordinator and dependency-blocked assignment, while distinguishing the unassigned idle agent.
Requests a bounded checkpoint and stops the coordinator when it does not respond in time.
Withholds ownership transfer and a replacement while the associated write operation remains active, reports the blocker, and continues independent authorized work.
Routes a fresh replacement only after all associated writes are confirmed stopped, reuses a healthy coordinator across ordinary merge waves, and does not claim integration or acceptance is complete.

evals.prompt: Describe decisions only, without running tools or dispatching. Worker A has reached its first deadline with no extensions. Its bounded checkpoint arrives on time with progress and an ETA. The parent chooses to extend. A later follow-up reports more progress, but the extended deadline then expires. Worker B reaches its first deadline and its checkpoint never arrives. Explain the sequence for both workers, including recorded state, enforcement and any replacement. Provide simulated fieldwise records and an action log for both workers, including conditions and routing for replacement; mark unknown values unresolved and do not claim execution.
evals.expected_output: At first expiry request status, completed work, blockers and ETA with a bounded deadline. For A record one ETA-based extension and re-arm; follow-up does not reset the count, and stop at extended expiry. For B stop on a late or absent checkpoint. Confirm each worker and associated write operations stopped before a fresh routed replacement; otherwise report the blocker without overlapping ownership.
assertions: Requests status, completed work, blockers and ETA with a bounded checkpoint deadline at first expiry.
Records the single ETA-based extension, increments its count and re-arms enforcement; the follow-up does not reset the count.
Stops A at the extended deadline and B when its checkpoint is late or absent, rather than granting another extension or waiting indefinitely.
Confirms each stopped worker and its associated writes are quiescent before transferring ownership to a fresh routed replacement; otherwise reports a blocker.

evals.prompt: Give a read-only orchestration decision; do not run tools or dispatch. At 10:00 the parent returns from a user interruption. Worker A's assignment deadline passed at 09:59; worker B is awaiting a checkpoint due at 10:01, and worker C has a running deadline at 10:04. Worker D finished on time and its evidence is available. The next review-fix task follows the prior review iteration, and the previously used, now idle agent was that iteration’s implementer. It matches the selected model exactly and was originally spawned without an effort override; the new task route is host_default. Explain the immediate decision, scheduling, any blocking operation, completion cleanup and what must be recorded for the new assignment. Provide draft assignment records and a simulated action log; mark unavailable values unresolved and do not claim enforcement or dispatch occurred.
evals.expected_output: Recheck all deadlines immediately and process A's expiry with a bounded checkpoint. Bound the next wait by the earliest active assignment or checkpoint deadline, including A's new checkpoint and B at 10:01, and independently time out operations that block enforcement. Cancel D's enforcement without treating worker completion as milestone acceptance. Reuse the previous review-fix iteration’s implementer because its model and omitted-effort configuration match the host_default route. For the reused agent create a fresh record including task and agent IDs, start, deadline, zero extensions and enforcement handle, and arm enforcement before waiting.
assertions: Rechecks deadlines after the interruption and initiates a bounded checkpoint for overdue A.
Bounds the next wait by the earliest active assignment or checkpoint deadline and independently times out operations blocking parent enforcement.
Cancels D's enforcement on completion and does not equate task completion with milestone acceptance.
Records the reused agent's new assignment ID, agent ID, start, deadline, zero extension count and enforcement handle or scheduler entry, and arms it before waiting.
Reuses the previous review-fix iteration’s implementer because its exact model and original omitted-effort configuration match the host_default route.

evals.prompt: Describe completion actions only; do not execute commands, dispatch agents, edit files, or remove worktrees. Every authorized task and milestone is resolved with acceptance evidence, final code review has no remaining issues, and every implementer worktree is clean with all changes integrated. The integration branch is feature/parser. Explain the final report and cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Report the resolved tasks and milestones and the integration branch feature/parser, then clean up all implementer worktrees.
assertions: Reports feature/parser as the integration branch and states that tasks and milestones are resolved.
Includes cleanup of all completed implementer worktrees.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not execute tools, dispatch, or edit. A dedicated implementer must materially redesign architecture and sequencing in an ExecPlan. The user explicitly chooses an exact model outside the recommended planning tier and asks for high effort. Host controls permit the model and high effort, and acceptance is confirmed. Explain the selection, effort policy, dispatch record, and deadline.
evals.expected_output: Honor the exact user model and explicit high effort, record explicit effort policy and the exact pair, and enforce the runtime deadline. The exact user model overrides the advisory tier while host restrictions still apply.
assertions: Uses the exact user-selected model over the advisory tier, subject to host restrictions.
Uses explicit high effort because the task is material planning and the user explicitly requested it.
Records the exact model/effort pair and preserves runtime deadline enforcement.
